label: conj:q-zero-stokes-region-identification
title: Substrate $q_0$ identification via Stokes region of the generating function (over $\mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]$)
html:
Conjecture. Substrate q_0 identification via Stokes region of the generating function (over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}])

Conjecture (Stokes region identification). The substrate parameter q_0 admits a canonical identification with a specific point on the geometric component of the character variety X(\mathcal{B}_3), realized via two dual perspectives that coincide by the AJ-conjecture machinery:

(a) Analytic / Stokes side: q_0 is the parameter value at which the Stokes region of the colored-Jones generating function G_K(x; q) = \sum J_N(K; q) \cdot x^N transitions between dilog-asymptotic regimes. (b) Algebraic / Hom-functor side: q_0 is the image under the archimedean realisation of a specific \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathbf{C}}-evaluation in the framework's brane-tower category \mathbf{C} over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{\pm 1}].

The two perspectives are related by QOU duality, which is exactly the AJ-conjecture machinery \hat{A}_K \cdot J_N = 0 in the q-Weyl algebra \mathcal{A}_q over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}].

Mostow-Prasad rigidity and Reid's trace field theorem guarantee a unique algebraic distinguished point [\rho_{\mathrm{DF}}]. The specific algebraic identification of q_0 as a particular invariant of [\rho_{\mathrm{DF}}] remains the conjectural gap. We use Stokes asymptotics to formalise this identification. The dilog-asymptotic regimes bounding the Stokes region are anchored by the \theta = \pi/3 saddle of \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(e^{i\theta}), computed once in the dilog saddle regime. The Iwahori-Hecke algebra H_n(q) and structural identities hold over the universal base \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{\pm 1}]. Physical observables are the images under the archimedean realisation \iota_\infty: \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{\pm 1}] \to \mathbb{R} at q := q_0.
